questions.question:
An IAM role has an identity-based policy that allows kms:Decrypt on a customer managed key in the same account. The key policy contains only the default statement for the key administrators and does not include the statement that enables IAM policies. Calls to Decrypt fail with AccessDenied.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Add a statement to the key policy that allows the account principal (arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:root) so that IAM policies can grant access, or grant the role directly in the key policy.
Create an SCP that allows kms:Decrypt for the role.
Attach the AWSKeyManagementServicePowerUser managed policy to the role.
Enable automatic key rotation, which resets the key permissions.

questions.explanation: En KMS, la key policy es la fuente principal de permisos: las políticas IAM solo funcionan si la key policy lo habilita (statement para la cuenta). Sin ese statement, ninguna política IAM otorga acceso.

questions.question:
A customer managed key must be usable by any principal in the account only when the request comes through Amazon S3 in us-east-1, and never through direct calls to AWS KMS.

Which condition should the key policy use?

options.text: aws:CalledVia with the value kms.amazonaws.com
aws:SourceVpce with the S3 gateway endpoint ID
kms:ViaService with the value s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
kms:CallerAccount with the account ID

questions.explanation: kms:ViaService limita el uso de la clave a solicitudes que un servicio de AWS concreto hace en nombre del principal. kms:CallerAccount solo limita la cuenta.

questions.question:
An application encrypts records with AWS KMS. The security team wants each Decrypt call to be bound to a specific tenant ID, so that ciphertext from one tenant cannot be decrypted in the context of another, and wants the tenant ID visible in CloudTrail.

What should the application use?

options.text: A separate AWS managed key for each tenant.
A grant token for each tenant.
The tenant ID as the key alias.
An encryption context that includes the tenant ID, optionally enforced with the kms:EncryptionContext condition key.

questions.explanation: El encryption context son datos autenticados adicionales: el Decrypt debe incluir el mismo contexto, aparece en CloudTrail y puede exigirse en políticas. Las AWS managed keys no se crean por tenant.

questions.question:
An application must encrypt files up to 2 GB with AWS KMS. Calls to the Encrypt API fail for these files.

What should the developer do?

options.text: Increase the KMS request quota for Encrypt.
Use an asymmetric KMS key, which supports larger payloads.
Use envelope encryption: call GenerateDataKey, encrypt the file locally with the plaintext data key, and store the encrypted data key with the file.
Split each file into 4 KB chunks and call Encrypt for each chunk.

questions.explanation: Encrypt acepta hasta 4 KB. Para datos grandes se usa envelope encryption con data keys (por ejemplo, con el AWS Encryption SDK). Dividir en 4 KB sería ineficiente y costoso.

questions.question:
A security engineer scheduled a customer managed key for deletion with a 30-day waiting period. The engineer is worried that some application might still use the key.

What should the engineer do to detect usage during the waiting period?

options.text: Use AWS Config to detect resources encrypted with the key.
Reduce the waiting period to 7 days so that failures appear sooner.
Create a CloudWatch alarm from a metric filter on CloudTrail events that detects requests failing because the key is pending deletion.
Enable automatic key rotation to keep a backup of the key material.

questions.explanation: Una clave pendiente de eliminación no se puede usar, y las solicitudes fallidas quedan en CloudTrail. Una alarma permite cancelar la eliminación a tiempo. Alternativa más segura: deshabilitar la clave primero.

questions.question:
A compliance standard requires rotating the key material of customer managed keys every 180 days, while continuing to decrypt data encrypted with previous key material without re-encrypting it.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Enable automatic key rotation on the symmetric customer managed keys with a rotation period of 180 days.
Use AWS managed keys, which rotate every 180 days.
Import new key material every 180 days into the same key.
Create a new key every 180 days and update the alias, then re-encrypt all data.

questions.explanation: La rotación automática admite periodos personalizados (90 a 2560 días) y conserva el material anterior para descifrar. Las AWS managed keys rotan cada año y no se configuran.

questions.question:
Regulations require that the company generate key material in its own on-premises HSM, be able to make the key unusable immediately, and keep a copy of the key material outside AWS. The keys are used with S3 and EBS.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a KMS key with an AWS_KMS origin and schedule it for deletion when needed.
Use a multi-Region key and delete the replica when needed.
Use an AWS CloudHSM cluster and export the keys to the on-premises HSM.
Create a KMS key with an EXTERNAL origin, import the key material from the on-premises HSM, and delete the imported key material when needed.

questions.explanation: Con material importado, la empresa genera la clave y puede borrar el material de inmediato (o fijarle expiración), conservando su copia. Programar la eliminación de una clave normal tiene un periodo de espera mínimo de 7 días.

questions.question:
A company encrypts data client-side in us-east-1 and replicates the ciphertext to eu-west-1 with DynamoDB global tables. In a disaster, the application in eu-west-1 must decrypt the data without calling AWS KMS in us-east-1.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Copy the key material from us-east-1 to eu-west-1 with the ExportKey API.
Use the AWS managed key aws/dynamodb in both Regions.
Create a separate single-Region key in eu-west-1 with the same alias.
Use a multi-Region KMS key with a replica in eu-west-1, which shares the same key ID and key material.

questions.explanation: Las claves multi-Region comparten material e ID, de modo que el ciphertext de una Región se descifra con la réplica en otra. Una clave distinta con el mismo alias tiene material diferente, y KMS no exporta material.

questions.question:
Regulations require that encryption keys be stored in single-tenant HSMs that the company controls exclusively, while still using KMS integration with AWS services such as EBS and S3.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS KMS custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster, and create KMS keys in it.
Use the default AWS KMS key store, which uses single-tenant HSMs.
Use AWS CloudHSM directly and configure S3 to call the HSM.
Use an external key store that points to AWS CloudHSM.

questions.explanation: El CloudHSM key store mantiene el material en HSMs single-tenant que controlas, y los servicios siguen usando KMS. El almacén por defecto de KMS es multi-tenant.

questions.question:
A company must keep its encryption keys physically outside AWS, in its own key manager, with the ability to deny all decryption of its AWS data by disconnecting the external key manager.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: A CloudHSM key store in the company's VPC.
An AWS KMS external key store (XKS) that connects to the company's external key manager through an XKS proxy.
Imported key material from the company's key manager.
Client-side encryption with keys stored in Secrets Manager.

questions.explanation: Con XKS las operaciones criptográficas se hacen en el gestor externo; si se desconecta, las claves no pueden usarse. Con material importado, el material sí reside en KMS. (XKS implica mayor latencia y menor disponibilidad.)

questions.question: Which statement about AWS CloudHSM is correct?

options.text: The customer manages HSM users and keys, and AWS cannot access or recover the keys if the customer loses the credentials.
CloudHSM keys rotate automatically every year.
CloudHSM is multi-tenant, and keys are isolated by IAM policies.
AWS manages the crypto users and can recover lost keys.

questions.explanation: En CloudHSM el cliente controla los usuarios y las claves en HSMs dedicados; AWS gestiona el hardware pero no tiene acceso a las claves.

questions.question:
A bucket uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key. KMS costs have increased significantly, and some applications are being throttled because of the high volume of KMS requests from S3.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Use DSSE-KMS, which uses fewer KMS calls.
Request a quota increase and disable CloudTrail data events.
Change the encryption to SSE-C.
Enable S3 Bucket Keys for SSE-KMS on the bucket.

questions.explanation: Las S3 Bucket Keys generan una clave a nivel de bucket que reduce las llamadas a KMS y su costo. DSSE-KMS aplica dos capas de cifrado y no reduce llamadas.

questions.question:
A company must ensure that every object uploaded to a bucket is encrypted with a specific customer managed key (not the AWS managed key or SSE-S3), even if a client specifies different encryption headers.

Which bucket policy statement meets this requirement?

options.text: Deny s3:PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id does not equal the ARN of the approved key.
Deny s3:PutObject when aws:SecureTransport is false.
Allow s3:PutObject only when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption equals AES256.
Deny s3:PutObject when the s3:x-amz-acl header is present.

questions.explanation: La condición sobre la key ID impide usar otra clave aunque el cliente la indique. AES256 corresponde a SSE-S3, y SecureTransport controla el cifrado en tránsito.

questions.question:
A bucket has 500 million objects encrypted with SSE-S3. The company changed the bucket's default encryption to SSE-KMS and must ensure that all existing objects are also encrypted with the new key.

Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Nothing; changing default encryption re-encrypts existing objects automatically.
Enable S3 Versioning, which creates encrypted versions automatically.
Use S3 Batch Operations with a copy operation that re-encrypts the objects in place with the KMS key.
Download all objects and upload them again with a script.

questions.explanation: La encriptación por defecto solo aplica a objetos nuevos. Batch Operations copia los objetos existentes con el nuevo cifrado a gran escala.

questions.question:
A regulation requires two independent layers of server-side encryption for certain objects stored in S3.

Which option meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use SSE-S3 and enable S3 Versioning.
Use SSE-KMS with S3 Bucket Keys.
Use SSE-C with two keys.
Use dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (DSSE-KMS).

questions.explanation: DSSE-KMS aplica dos capas independientes de cifrado del lado del servidor. SSE-C solo usa una clave por solicitud.

questions.question:
A company has an unencrypted Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in production. A new policy requires encryption at rest.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Create an encrypted read replica from the unencrypted instance and promote it.
Create a snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled using a KMS key, and restore a new encrypted DB instance from the copy, then switch the application.
Enable EBS encryption by default in the Region.
Modify the DB instance and enable encryption.

questions.explanation: El cifrado de RDS se define al crear la instancia; para cifrar una existente se copia un snapshot con cifrado y se restaura. No se pueden crear réplicas cifradas de una instancia sin cifrar.

questions.question:
The security team must ensure that every new EBS volume and snapshot copy in the account is encrypted, even if a developer forgets to request encryption.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Use a bucket policy that requires encryption for EBS.
Enable EBS encryption by default in every Region used, optionally with a customer managed key as the default.
Create an AWS Config rule that deletes unencrypted volumes.
Attach an SCP that denies ec2:CreateSnapshot.

questions.explanation: El cifrado por defecto de EBS es una configuración por Región que cifra automáticamente los volúmenes nuevos. (Puede reforzarse con políticas declarativas o SCP con ec2:Encrypted.)

questions.question:
A company must copy encrypted RDS snapshots from us-east-1 to us-west-2 for disaster recovery.

Which requirement applies to the copy?

options.text: The same single-Region key ARN must be used in both Regions.
A KMS key in the destination Region (us-west-2) must be specified, because KMS keys are Regional (unless a multi-Region key is used).
The snapshot must be decrypted before the copy.
Encrypted snapshots cannot be copied between Regions.

questions.explanation: Las KMS keys son regionales: la copia en otra Región se cifra con una clave de esa Región.

questions.question:
A company must ensure that all traffic between EC2 instances within its VPCs is encrypted in transit, without modifying applications, and must be able to identify any resources whose traffic cannot be encrypted.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy Network Firewall with TLS inspection between all instances.
Use Nitro-based instance types that support automatic in-transit encryption and enable VPC Encryption Controls in monitor mode, then enforce mode.
Use security groups that allow only port 443.
Enable EBS encryption by default.

questions.explanation: Los tipos Nitro compatibles cifran el tráfico entre instancias automáticamente. VPC Encryption Controls (2025) permite auditar (monitor) y exigir (enforce) cifrado en tránsito en la VPC.

questions.question:
An Application Load Balancer must accept only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 connections with strong ciphers, and the traffic between the ALB and the targets must also be encrypted.

Which configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an HTTP listener and enable encryption on the target group.
Use the ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08 policy and HTTP targets.
Use a TCP listener on port 443 and enable TLS on the security group.
Use an HTTPS listener with a TLS 1.3 security policy that supports TLS 1.2 (for example, ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06) and configure the target group with the HTTPS protocol.

questions.explanation: La security policy del listener define protocolos y cifrados permitidos; un target group HTTPS cifra el tramo ALB-destino.

questions.question:
A B2B API behind an Application Load Balancer must authenticate partner systems with client certificates issued by the company's private CA.

Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener and security groups.
Use an AWS WAF rule that inspects the client certificate.
Terminate TLS on the targets and implement certificate validation in the application.
Enable mutual TLS on the ALB HTTPS listener in verify mode with a trust store that contains the private CA certificate.

questions.explanation: El ALB soporta mTLS en modo verify con trust stores, validando los certificados de cliente sin código en la aplicación.

questions.question:
A company imported a third-party certificate into ACM for its ALB. Last year the certificate expired unexpectedly and caused an outage.

What should the security engineer do to prevent this?

options.text: Enable managed renewal for the imported certificate in ACM.
Use AWS Config to renew the certificate automatically.
Increase the certificate validity in the ALB listener.
Create an EventBridge rule for ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration events (or a CloudWatch alarm on DaysToExpiry) and notify the team, because ACM does not renew imported certificates.

questions.explanation: ACM renueva automáticamente sus propios certificados, pero no los importados; hay que monitorear la expiración con eventos o métricas.

questions.question:
A security engineer wants to use an ACM public certificate with a CloudFront distribution, but the certificate does not appear in the CloudFront console.

What is the cause?

options.text: Public ACM certificates cannot be used with CloudFront.
The certificate must be exported and uploaded to CloudFront.
The certificate was requested in a Region other than us-east-1; certificates for CloudFront must be in us-east-1.
The certificate must use email validation.

questions.explanation: CloudFront solo usa certificados de ACM de la Región us-east-1.

questions.question:
Microservices in several accounts need TLS certificates for internal service-to-service communication. Certificates should be valid for only a few days to reduce the need for revocation, and costs must be minimized.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use ACM public certificates for internal names.
Use self-signed certificates generated by each service.
Use AWS Private CA in general-purpose mode with a CRL for each certificate.
Use AWS Private CA in short-lived certificate mode, shared with the other accounts through AWS RAM.

questions.explanation: El modo short-lived certificate de Private CA es más económico para certificados de corta vida (hasta 7 días). La CA se comparte entre cuentas con RAM. ACM público no emite para nombres internos.

questions.question:
A company is designing a private PKI with AWS Private CA. The security team wants to minimize the impact if the CA that issues end-entity certificates is compromised.

Which design follows best practices?

options.text: Create a root CA that is used only to sign subordinate CAs, and issue end-entity certificates from a subordinate CA.
Export the root CA private key and store it in S3.
Create a different root CA for each certificate.
Issue all certificates directly from a single root CA.

questions.explanation: Una jerarquía con raíz y subordinadas permite revocar una subordinada comprometida sin reemplazar la raíz. Las claves privadas de Private CA no se pueden exportar.

questions.question:
An application uses a database password stored in Secrets Manager. The company requires automatic rotation every 30 days without application downtime, even if a client still uses the previous password briefly.

Which rotation strategy should the security engineer use?

options.text: Manual rotation by a database administrator.
Single user rotation with a 30-day schedule.
Alternating users rotation, which alternates between two database users so that the previous credentials remain valid until the next rotation.
Store the password in Parameter Store SecureString with automatic rotation.

questions.explanation: La estrategia de usuarios alternos mantiene válidas las credenciales anteriores durante la rotación; con un solo usuario puede haber una breve ventana con fallos. Parameter Store no tiene rotación nativa.

questions.question:
A Lambda function in Account A must read a secret stored in Secrets Manager in Account B. The secret is encrypted with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager.

What must the security engineer do?

options.text: Re-encrypt the secret with a customer managed key that allows Account A, add a resource policy to the secret that allows the Lambda role, and allow the role in its identity-based policy.
Grant the Lambda role access to the aws/secretsmanager key in Account B.
Add only a resource policy to the secret that allows the Lambda role.
Share the secret with AWS RAM.

questions.explanation: Para acceso entre cuentas se requieren la resource policy del secreto, la política de identidad y una customer managed key compartida; la AWS managed key no permite acceso entre cuentas.

questions.question:
A company runs an application in us-east-1 and a disaster recovery copy in us-west-2. Both copies must use the same database credentials, and rotation must happen only once.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Parameter Store in both Regions with the same parameter name.
Configure the secret in us-east-1 to replicate to us-west-2; rotation of the primary secret updates the replica.
Create two independent secrets and rotate both with the same Lambda function.
Store the credentials in an S3 bucket with cross-Region replication.

questions.explanation: La replicación de secretos mantiene réplicas sincronizadas en otras Regiones; la rotación se hace en el secreto primario.

questions.question:
Developers hardcoded database credentials in application code. The security team wants to find these secrets in Lambda functions and EC2 instances automatically.

Which service can detect hardcoded secrets in Lambda function code?

options.text: Amazon Inspector Lambda code scanning.
Amazon Macie.
AWS Secrets Manager rotation.
GuardDuty Lambda Protection.

questions.explanation: El escaneo de código de Lambda de Inspector detecta secretos codificados y vulnerabilidades en el código. Macie analiza S3, y GuardDuty Lambda Protection monitoriza la actividad de red.

questions.question:
An SNS topic distributes order events to several subscribers. One subscriber (an analytics system) must not receive credit card numbers, while the payment service must receive them.

Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a Lambda function that removes card numbers before publishing.
Create two topics and publish twice from the producer.
Configure an SNS message data protection policy with a de-identify (mask) statement for the analytics subscription endpoint.
Use a subscription filter policy that drops messages with card numbers.

questions.explanation: La protección de datos de mensajes de SNS puede auditar, desidentificar (enmascarar) o denegar datos sensibles por publicador o suscriptor.

questions.question:
The security team wants to know how often PII appears in CloudWatch Logs across all log groups in the account and receive findings, without masking yet.

What should the security engineer configure?

options.text: An Amazon Macie job on the log groups.
An account-level CloudWatch Logs data protection policy with an audit destination (for example, S3 or CloudWatch Logs).
A metric filter for each log group.
A Config rule for each log group.

questions.explanation: Las data protection policies pueden configurarse a nivel de cuenta y enviar hallazgos de auditoría a un destino. Macie no analiza CloudWatch Logs.

questions.question:
A financial company must retain trade records in S3 for 7 years in a WORM format. Nobody, including the root user, can delete them during that time, and the bucket is new.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable Object Lock in governance mode and restrict s3:BypassGovernanceRetention.
Use a bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject.
Create the bucket with Object Lock enabled and set a default retention of 7 years in compliance mode.
Enable S3 Versioning and MFA Delete.

questions.explanation: El modo compliance no permite que nadie (ni root) borre ni acorte la retención. Governance puede eludirse con un permiso, y una bucket policy puede modificarse.

questions.question:
A legal team must prevent deletion of specific objects that are relevant to a lawsuit, with no known end date. Other objects in the bucket follow normal retention.

What should the security engineer use?

options.text: A compliance-mode retention period of 100 years on the bucket.
S3 Object Lock legal holds on the specific objects.
S3 Lifecycle rules that exclude the objects.
A Glacier Vault Lock policy.

questions.explanation: Un legal hold impide borrar una versión de objeto hasta que se retire, sin fecha de expiración, e independiente del periodo de retención.

questions.question:
A company wants protection against ransomware that could compromise administrator credentials in the production account. Backups must be impossible to delete, even by the backup account's root user, once configured.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode in the production account.
Copy backups to a vault in a dedicated backup account and apply AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode after the grace period.
Increase the backup retention period to 10 years.
Encrypt the backups with a customer managed key in the production account.

questions.explanation: Vault Lock en modo compliance se vuelve inmutable al terminar el periodo de gracia (cooling-off); ni root puede eliminar los recovery points ni la configuración. Separar la cuenta añade aislamiento.

questions.question:
A company wants an isolated backup copy that is stored in a vault encrypted with an AWS-owned key, locked in compliance mode, and that can be shared with a recovery account through AWS RAM for fast restore.

Which AWS Backup feature meets these requirements?

options.text: AWS Backup Audit Manager.
A logically air-gapped vault.
Cross-Region copy to a standard vault.
A standard backup vault with Vault Lock in governance mode.

questions.explanation: Los logically air-gapped vaults están bloqueados en modo compliance, cifrados con claves de AWS y pueden compartirse con RAM para restaurar desde otra cuenta.

questions.question:
A company must ensure that every account in the organization backs up resources tagged backup=daily, and must prove compliance to auditors.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use EBS snapshots scheduled with Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager in each account.
Create backup plans in each account with a script.
Use AWS Config rules to create backups.
Use AWS Organizations backup policies to deploy backup plans to all accounts, and use AWS Backup Audit Manager frameworks to report compliance.

questions.explanation: Las backup policies de Organizations aplican planes de respaldo de forma centralizada, y Backup Audit Manager genera evidencia de cumplimiento.

questions.question:
The security team must ensure that only code from trusted publishers can be deployed to Lambda functions, and that code modified after signing is rejected.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Signer signing profiles and a Lambda code signing configuration with the untrusted artifact policy set to Enforce.
Use S3 Object Lock on the deployment bucket.
Use KMS to encrypt the deployment package.
Use an SCP that denies lambda:UpdateFunctionCode.

questions.explanation: Con code signing, Lambda verifica la firma e integridad del paquete y, en modo Enforce, rechaza código no firmado o modificado.

questions.question: Which actions are required to replicate objects encrypted with SSE-KMS to a bucket in another Region? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use the same single-Region key in both Regions
Specify a KMS key in the destination Region in the replication configuration
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Disable encryption on the source bucket
Grant the replication role permission to decrypt with the source key and encrypt with the destination key

questions.explanation: La replicación de objetos SSE-KMS debe habilitarse explícitamente, indicando la clave de destino; el rol necesita kms:Decrypt en origen y kms:Encrypt en destino.

questions.question: Which practices reduce the risk of accidental or malicious loss of a customer managed KMS key? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Grant kms:* to all developers to avoid outages
Store the key material in an S3 bucket
Separate key administrators from key users in the key policy
Disable keys before deleting them and monitor usage
Deny kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion except for a break-glass role
Use the minimum 7-day waiting period for all deletions

questions.explanation: Separar funciones, restringir la eliminación y deshabilitar antes de borrar previenen pérdidas irrecuperables. El material de una clave de KMS no se puede exportar.

questions.question: Order the steps to encrypt an existing unencrypted EBS volume attached to an EC2 instance.

options.text: Create a snapshot of the unencrypted volume
Copy the snapshot with encryption enabled using a KMS key
Create a new volume from the encrypted snapshot
Stop the instance, detach the old volume, and attach the new encrypted volume

questions.explanation: No se puede cifrar un volumen existente directamente; se pasa por un snapshot cifrado.

questions.question: Order the steps of envelope encryption for a large file with AWS KMS.

options.text: Call GenerateDataKey with the KMS key
Encrypt the file locally with the plaintext data key
Discard the plaintext data key from memory
Store the encrypted data key together with the encrypted file

questions.explanation: Para descifrar se llama a Decrypt con la data key cifrada y se usa la data key en claro localmente.

questions.question: Match each requirement with the MOST appropriate key option.

prompts.text: Keys in single-tenant HSMs, integrated with KMS
Keys must remain physically outside AWS
Generate key material on premises, delete it from AWS immediately
Decrypt the same ciphertext in two Regions
Lowest overhead for an AWS service's default encryption

options.text: Multi-Region key
Key stored in Parameter Store
Imported key material
External key store (XKS)
CloudHSM key store
AWS managed key

questions.explanation: Cada opción de KMS responde a requisitos distintos de control, ubicación y operación.

questions.question: Match each immutability need with the feature that meets it.

prompts.text: WORM objects that nobody can delete for a fixed period
Hold objects for litigation without an end date
Backups that cannot be deleted after the grace period

options.text: AWS Signer with Lambda code signing
AWS Backup Vault Lock compliance mode
S3 Object Lock compliance mode
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Object Lock legal hold

questions.explanation: Cada mecanismo aporta inmutabilidad en un ámbito distinto; Transfer Acceleration solo acelera las cargas.

questions.question:
A bucket policy must deny any request that is not sent over HTTPS.

Which condition should the Deny statement use?

options.text: "Bool": {"aws:SecureTransport": "true"}
"NumericLessThan": {"s3:TlsVersion": "1.0"}
"Bool": {"aws:SecureTransport": "false"}
"StringEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}

questions.explanation: aws:SecureTransport es false en solicitudes sin TLS. (Para exigir una versión mínima de TLS también existe s3:TlsVersion, pero sería NumericLessThan 1.2.)

questions.question:
Clients connect to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The security team must ensure that the database rejects any connection that does not use TLS.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Set the rds.force_ssl parameter to 1 in the DB parameter group.
Add a security group rule that allows only port 443.
Enable IAM database authentication.
Enable encryption at rest on the DB instance.

questions.explanation: rds.force_ssl (PostgreSQL) o require_secure_transport (MySQL) obligan a usar TLS en las conexiones. El cifrado en reposo no afecta al tránsito.
